title: Launch flags that matter
hook: There are over a hundred flags. A handful decide your memory, your cache and your attention. Read what each really does in the source, and leave the rest alone.

verified.claim: Flag names, groups and help text are from the source.
The real parser refuses --highvram with --lowvram, --use-sage-attention with --use-flash-attention, and --cache-none with --cache-classic.
verified.ref: comfy/cli_args.py parser, run without starting a server

verified.claim: enables_dynamic_vram's rule and main.py's further support checks.
The default cache is RAM pressure, keeping 10% of system RAM free, at least 2 GB and at most 10 GB.
The attention choice follows the order in the Lab.
--reserve-vram sets EXTRA_RESERVED_VRAM, which also raises minimum_inference_memory.
The graph ran on a CPU.

unchecked: We did not benchmark any flag. Whether one helps depends on the card, the driver and the graph.
How --vram-headroom behaves in comfy-aimdo, which we did not read. We report only its help text.
The port of the attention order assumes no xformers, which changes the result where it is installed. AMD and other cards have further branches we left out.
